title: Avalon Health - Redwood Onboarding Kickoff
meeting_header: 2026-04-01 16:00 - 16:55 UTC | Duration: 55m | Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Maya Gonzalez (Redwood CSM), Dmitri Ivanov (Redwood SE), Rachel Moore (Avalon Head of Data), Anil Kapoor (Avalon CTO), Samantha Price (Avalon Platform)
summary: Introductory onboarding kickoff for Avalon Health. Covered success criteria, current stack (AWS EKS, private VPC), security/compliance needs (SOC 2, HIPAA, data residency), recommended Redwood deployment options (hosted for initial pilot, move to Dedicated/Private for PHI workloads), pilot scope (user-facing assistant for care coordination), timeline (pilot in 6 weeks), and immediate next steps: share security package, pricing, setup trial org, schedule technical benchmark check-in.
topics: Deployment mode discussion: hosted vs dedicated vs private
Pilot scope and metrics (latency, cost, accuracy)
next_steps: Redwood to send security pack + SOC2 summary (Maya)
Redwood to send pilot pricing options and Dedicated/Private comparison (Jordan)
Schedule SE-led benchmark session for 2026-04-08 to test latency with Avalon prompt set (Dmitri)
Avalon to provision test datasets and whitelist IPs for trial (Samantha)
Set up Redwood trial org and invite Avalon users (Maya)
Follow-up meeting in 1 week to confirm timelines and sign-off pilot scope
action_items: Maya Gonzalez - share security package & SOC2 summary (due: 2026-04-03)
Jordan Lee - send pilot pricing and Dedicated vs Private pros/cons doc (due: 2026-04-02)
Dmitri Ivanov - run initial benchmark plan & propose test times (due: 2026-04-06)
Samantha Price - share infra diagrams and whitelist IPs (due: 2026-04-05)
Rachel Moore - provide sample prompt set and success metrics (due: 2026-04-04)
transcript: 00:00 Jordan: hi everyone, thanks for joining. i'm jordan lee from redwood, our ae. maya and dmitri are here too. quick intros?
00:08 Rachel: hey, rachel moore here, head of data at avalon. excited to get started.
00:12 Anil: anil kapoor, cto. we'll be owning infrastructure side.
00:17 Samantha: samantha price, platform eng, i'll handle network/permissions.
00:22 Maya: maya gonzalez, customer success at redwood, i'll help with onboarding and timelines.
00:28 Dmitri: dmitri ivanov, solutions engineer, i'll lead technical integration and benchmarks.
00:35 Jordan: great. agenda — confirm success criteria, security, pilot scope, timeline, next steps. feel free to interrupt.

01:02 Rachel: high level — our goal is to ship a care coordination assistant that summaries patient messages and suggests next steps, reduce manual touch by 30 percent. latency target under 200ms token time ideally, not sure that's realistic, and cost per convo under $0.10 target, rough numbers.

01:28 Jordan: love that. typical Redwood levers are batching, kv cache, and quantization — we can tune cost/latency. for pilot we recommend hosted api to move fast, then dedicated or private for PHI. any regulatory constraints?

01:45 Anil: yes, we handle PHI. HIPAA compliance is required. we run most services in us-east-1, data residency must stay in us regions. we also need audit logs, sso, and key management. is redwood — is there a private offering?

02:12 Maya: yes, we have Redwood Private (vpc/on-prem option) with customer-managed KMS and audit logs. for pilot we can use hosted with data controls and retention settings, but for production with PHI we recommend Private or Dedicated with kms integration.
02:35 Samantha: ok that makes sense. for the pilot can we do a non-PHI dataset first and run benchmarks? we want to validate latency and QA before moving to private.

02:44 Dmitri: absolutely. typical flow is: test on hosted with synthetic or scrubbed data, run benchmarks, then move to Dedicated/Private for production. i'll run a bench that simulates your convo lengths and top-k prompts. any specific seq len?
03:08 Rachel: average prompt+context ~700 tokens, but we have cases up to 2k with attachments. for now pilot use up to 1k.

03:20 Dmitri: ok. i'll size batches and test the model variants. do you have a preferred model? open to recommendations — we can propose 2 variants: a smaller, faster quantized model for latency, and a larger for quality.
03:34 Anil: quality > cost for initial pilot but latency still important. what's the turnaround for model recommendations?
03:40 Dmitri: i can propose profiles within 48 hours, will include expected p50/p95 latencies and token cost estimates.
04:05 Jordan: quick question on auth — do you manage users via okta?
04:12 Samantha: yes okta sso, want role-based access, admin-only for config. also need audit logs retained for 1 year.
04:22 Maya: we support sso/saml and rbac, and retention settings can be adjusted. for long-term retention we offer add-on observability retention if needed.
04:35 Rachel: and encryption at rest — we need customer-managed keys for production.
04:40 Maya: yep, kms/hsm integration is available on Private and Dedicated plans, we can add docs in the security pack.
05:05 Anil: legal will review data processing and dpa — any standard templates?
05:12 Jordan: we'll share our DPA + SOC2 summary. maya will attach the security dossier after this call.
05:18 Samantha: also, network — we prefer VPC peering or private link. do you support private endpoints?
05:26 Dmitri: we support VPC peering, private link and on-prem connectors depending on the environment. i'll list network options in the bench plan doc.
05:50 Rachel: good. timeline — we're aiming for a 6 week pilot, with a sign-off at the end where we validate latency and a decrease in manual triage. are those things you can commit to?

06:05 Maya: 6 weeks is reasonable. typical milestones: week 1 setup/trial provisioning, week 2 ingest prompts & test data, weeks 3-4 benchmarks and tuning, week 5 pilot run, week 6 evaluation and decision point.
06:34 Anil: budget question — will pricing be usage based or reserved?
06:40 Jordan: for pilot we usually do usage-based, then present reserved/dedicated options if you want predictable capacity/cost. i'll send a comparison sheet.
07:02 Rachel: any integrations for our internal ticketing system (zendesk) to route suggestions?
07:10 Dmitri: yes we have webhook and api patterns plus example lambda connectors; we'll share a reference repo link.
07:28 Samantha: ok please share sample code; we prefer python snippets.
07:35 Jordan: noted — will include python snippets and a quickstart template in the trial invite.
08:00 Anil: security/pen test — do you do regular third-party pen tests?
08:06 Maya: we do annual third-party assessments and can share summary reports in the security pack. for private/on-prem we can run joint tests as needed.
08:22 Rachel: excellent. any immediate blockers from our side?
08:28 Samantha: we need IP ranges to be whitelisted and a contract review window, legal is backed up so expect 2 weeks, okay for pilot to start while legal reviews.
08:40 Maya: that's fine — pilot org can be provisioned for your engineers to test while legal finalizes terms.

09:01 Jordan: let's capture concrete next steps: i'll send pricing and pilot scope, maya will send security docs, dmitri will set up a benchmark plan for next week. can we tentatively schedule bench on 2026-04-08?
09:15 Anil: 4/8 works for us in the morning, can you do 10am ET?
09:20 Dmitri: 10am ET for bench session is fine, i'll send calendar invite.
09:40 Rachel: one more — are there any known limitations with attachments & pdf parsing? we plan to include structured forms.
09:47 Dmitri: attachments currently need pre-processing, we have connector patterns to extract text. for structured forms we recommend a separate parser step followed by the model prompt.
10:05 Samantha: ok we'll prep sample docs and share them via secure s3 link.
10:20 Jordan: wrapping up — recap of action items and owners. thanks everyone, we'll follow up by tomorrow with the security pack and pricing.
10:35 Rachel: thanks team, talk soon.
10:40 Meeting ended
